task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a business news story for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 11, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Broadreach Capital Partners completed its $380 million acquisition of Tribune Valley Media Group, giving the private equity firm ownership of 14 regional newspapers across the rural Midwest.
Tribune Valley's 14 papers have a combined paid circulation of approximately 340,000, including daily and Sunday editions.
Tribune Valley was founded in 1964 and has been owned by the Larkin family since its founding; the family sold its controlling stake as part of the acquisition.
Broadreach announced that 85 editorial positions would be eliminated, representing approximately 22 percent of Tribune Valley's 390-person editorial staff.
Broadreach managing partner Jeffrey Crane said: "Sustainable local journalism requires operating discipline that a family ownership structure can no longer afford in this environment."

Tribune Valley CEO Sarah Holloway, who will remain as chief executive, said in an internal memo obtained by reporters: "I will not sign off on cuts that destroy the editorial capacity of these papers."
Holloway's statement stopped short of threatening resignation.

The Newspaper Guild Local 203 represents journalists at six of the 14 Tribune Valley papers; the Guild filed an objection with the NLRB in February, arguing Broadreach failed to bargain over the announced job cuts.
Tribune Valley's digital advertising revenue totaled $42 million in 2024, an increase of 18 percent from 2023.
The company's print advertising revenue fell 31 percent over the same period.
The acquisition was reviewed by the Department of Justice before closing; the DOJ did not challenge it.

Broadreach has previously acquired two other regional newspaper groups; both experienced editorial staff reductions of more than 30 percent within 18 months of acquisition, according to journalism industry records.
Crane said Broadreach intends to invest in digital infrastructure for the papers but declined to specify an amount.
Three of Tribune Valley's papers have won regional journalism awards in the past two years; two investigations resulted in county-level official resignations.
The Local News Alliance, an advocacy organization, called the acquisition "the latest chapter in a pattern of private equity consolidation that has hollowed out local newsrooms."
The Local News Alliance estimates that Tribune Valley papers are the primary source of local news for approximately 510,000 residents in communities with no other local news outlet.
The acquisition price of $380 million is approximately 2.7 times Tribune Valley's 2024 revenue of $141 million.
Several Tribune Valley journalists reached by reporters said they would seek other positions if the job cuts proceeded as announced.
Tribune Valley is headquartered in fictional Clayfield, Iowa.
Broadreach declined to answer questions about editorial policies or whether Tribune Valley papers would share content across titles after the acquisition.
